# Local radial simplex descent in arbitrary integer and continuous dimensions

This theorem extends `candidate 65cb1818e941a654` to every continuous dimension d>=2. It proves an actual all-normal, all-source local formula, exact affine-radius escapes, and the rank of the normalized mass Hessian. The general formula is a uniquely attained finite polynomial minimum, not the residual square available in d=2. All families here start with centrally symmetric sampled radii and normalized depth Gamma_d. This is a restricted local theorem, not OC or a bound on the number of required ownership groups.

## 1. The bodies and theorem

Let n>=0, d>=2. Let B be a compact convex body in R^n such that P=B intersect Z^n is finite, centrally symmetric, and contains 0. Let r^0:B -> (0,infinity) be continuous and concave, with even sampled values r^0_z=r^0_-z. Define the centered simplex

    T_d=conv{v_0,...,v_d},
    v_0=(-1,...,-1),  v_i=v_0+(d+1)e_i,
    V_d=|T_d|=(d+1)^d/d!,
    Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d,
    c_d=Gamma_d V_d=d^d/d!.

For any positive continuous concave radius r on B, use the ACTUAL body

    C_r={(z,x): z in B, x in r(z)T_d},
    S_r=C_r intersect (Z^n x R^d).

It is compact and convex, has nonempty ambient interior, and its complete integer fibers are r_z T_d, z in P. The convexity proof is the equality

    t r(z)T_d+(1-t)r(w)T_d
       =[t r(z)+(1-t)r(w)]T_d subset r(tz+(1-t)w)T_d.

All fibers are positive dimensional d-bodies. Thus q=d, H_d(S_r)=V_d sum_z r_z^d, and every nonvertical hyperplane has zero H_d-measure in S_r. Put L=span(P) and k=dim L. All integer normal parameters below are restricted to L; perpendicular components are invisible on S_r.

For every compatible radius array sufficiently close to r^0, there is a unique small beta(r) in L satisfying

    sum_z z [d r_z+beta(r).z]^(d-1)=0.               (1)

Every bracket here is positive. Define

    tau(r)=(1/d!) sum_z [d r_z+beta(r).z]^d.         (2)

Then the unique globally deepest point of S_r is Y=(0,0), and its raw depth is exactly tau(r). Its complete minimizing trace menu consists of the d+1 canonical caps

    u_i.x+beta(r).z>=0,
    u_i=e_i (1<=i<=d),  u_0=-sum_(i=1)^d e_i.       (3)

Every other fiber centroid has strictly smaller actual depth. A finite orbit of one actual attaining cap under the simplex vertex-permutation group is a positive balanced family of critical caps covering that source's whole fiber. Assign each auxiliary family only its own base, and (3) only base 0. This is a complete finite ownership cover with strict budget slack at all auxiliary groups.

Let R_0=sum_z (r^0_z)^d and Q_0=c_d R_0. A common continuous homothety of factor [Q_0/tau(r)]^(1/d) gives an actual body of global raw depth Q_0 and total mass

    M_tilde(r)=V_d [sum_z r_z^d] Q_0/tau(r).        (4)

It is at least V_d R_0, with equality EXACTLY when

    sum_z r_z^(d-1) z=0.                            (5)

At the baseline, for a sampled radius velocity v=(v_z), put

    w_z=(r^0_z)^(d-2),
    G_w=sum_z w_z z z^T,
    m(v)=sum_z w_z v_z z.

The normalized mass Hessian is

    M_tilde''[v,v]
       =V_d d(d-1) m(v)^T G_w^dagger m(v).          (6)

It has rank k on the full sampled-array space, with kernel m(v)=0. Every affine mode a.z with a in L is actually compatible on the entire projection B. For sufficiently small a, it has the exact stronger properties

    r_a(z)=r^0(z)+a.z,
    beta(r_a)=-d a,
    tau(r_a)=Q_0,
    H_d(S_(r_a))=V_d sum_z [r^0_z+a.z]^d
                  >V_d R_0  if a!=0.              (7)

The gain is therefore genuinely available in k independent directions, rather than merely a positive form on unrealizable sampled velocities.

## 2. The finite-base compactness input and baseline cap menu

Section 2 of `candidate 65cb1818e941a654` gives an elementary uniform finite-base normal representation. Its proof is dimension independent. With a strict common support bound H and |u|=1, a cap

    u.x+alpha.(z-z_0)>=0

can have alpha replaced by a uniformly bounded coefficient preserving all fiber traces: retain alpha.(z-z_0) exactly inside [-H,H], impose the matching saturation inequalities outside, and choose the minimum-norm point in the resulting nonempty polyhedron. Its active-row basis comes from the fixed finite base matrix, so its norm is at most K(P)H. Strict support bounds preserve full and empty traces as sets. Compactness plus null hyperplane boundaries then gives continuous cap masses and attained nonvertical minima at all source centroids. Every purely vertical cap is strictly dominated by a sufficiently large finite integer tilt with a nonzero continuous normal: its nonboundary fiber statuses stay fixed, its boundary fibers become subsets, and its own centroid fiber loses positive volume. This retains every closed ambient halfspace, including those with whole-fiber boundary mass.

Uniformly over ALL fixed halfspaces H',

    |mu_r(H')-mu_s(H')|
       <=V_d sum_z |r_z^d-s_z^d|.                  (8)

This is the exact symmetric-difference measure of the nested homothetic fibers, so it needs no boundedness of the original halfspace parameters. One common support bound and one compact representation work in a sampled-radius neighborhood.

We use two previously proved and independently audited ordinary statements, neither of which assumes OC:

1. The paired centroid-tail inequality from `candidate 732b11a769399016`: for any d-body K with centroid 0, every u!=0 and t in R,

       |K intersect {u.x>=t}|+|K intersect {u.x>=-t}|
          >=2 Gamma_d |K|.

2. The ordinary simplex centroid minimum is Gamma_d and its only minimizing normals are the d+1 apex-side facet-parallel ones. The full equality proof is in `candidate e2c55c91458e1e8c`; its explicit simplex cap consequence is also stated in `candidate 3795aff5f3322d52`, Section 2.

Pairing z and -z at Y, and counting the positive own fiber once, yields raw_depth(Y)>=Q_0. The canonical cylinders u_i.x>=0 attain Q_0 and cover EVERY fiber space, so the actual baseline global maximum is Q_0.

The own centroid fiber forces every equality continuous normal to be canonical by statement 2. For a reflected equal-radius pair, let s=|alpha.z|. If 0<s<=r_z, both canonical traces are proper and their total is

    [(d r_z+s)^d+(d r_z-s)^d]/d!
       >2(d r_z)^d/d!,                             (9)

by strict convexity of t^d on positive t. If s>=r_z, one trace is full and the total is at least V_d r_z^d>2 Gamma_d V_d r_z^d. The latter inequality uses Gamma_d<1/2 for d>=2; equivalently (1+1/d)^d>2 by its binomial expansion. Thus equality forces alpha.z=0 for every base, or alpha=0 on L. This proves the COMPLETE baseline active trace menu, not merely a displayed collection of caps. The common compact representation gives a strict mass gap outside small neighborhoods of these d+1 directions.

## 3. Every competing source is strictly shallower

Every permutation of the d+1 vertices acts by a linear volume-preserving map on T_d. These maps act simultaneously on all radial fibers. The average of the full permutation orbit of any point is zero: its barycentric coordinates average to 1/(d+1). Depth superlevel sets are convex, because every halfspace containing a convex combination contains at least one combined point. Consequently each fiber's depth is maximized at its actual centroid:

    raw_depth(z,x)<=raw_depth(z,0).                 (10)

Fix a nonzero z_0 in P. The canonical cylinder x_1>=0 has mass Q_0. In its proper through-source tilt chamber the exact mass is

    (1/d!) sum_z [d r^0_z+alpha.(z-z_0)]^d.

Its alpha-gradient at zero equals

    c_d sum_z (r^0_z)^(d-1)(z-z_0)
       =-c_d z_0 sum_z (r^0_z)^(d-1),              (11)

which is nonzero. Taking alpha=t z_0 for sufficiently small t>0 strictly decreases this polynomial. Such a choice remains proper because the finite list of initial cuts is proper with positive margins. This proves a strict actual depth gap at every nonzero source and, by (10), throughout its fiber. The minimum of these finitely many positive gaps is positive. Inequality (8) preserves a positive gap in a sampled-radius neighborhood.

At base 0, a nonzero x has u_i.x>0 for some canonical normal since sum u_i=0 and the u_i span R^d. Shift this canonical cap upward to pass through x. It loses positive own-fiber volume and cannot gain volume elsewhere. Thus Y is the unique baseline global maximizer. The same argument will apply to the optimized canonical caps below.

## 4. Exact angular optimization

Work near the vertex cap with continuous normal e_1. Write a through-Y plane as

    x_1+sum_(j=2)^d theta_j x_j+alpha.z>=0.

For small theta, alpha, and sampled-radius changes, its trace in every original fiber remains a proper one-vertex cap. Its peak height at r_z v_1 is

    [d-sum_(j=2)^d theta_j]r_z+alpha.z.

The d edge drops from v_1 are (d+1)r_z and (d+1)(1-theta_j)r_z, j=2,...,d. Multiplying their intercept fractions against the full simplex volume gives the exact ACTUAL cap formula

    Phi(r,alpha,theta)
      = sum_z { [d-sum theta_j]r_z+alpha.z }^d
          /[d! product_(j=2)^d(1-theta_j)].         (12)

Put s=1-(sum theta_j)/d>0 and beta=alpha/s. Then

    Phi=A(theta) F_r(beta),
    F_r(beta)=(1/d!)sum_z[d r_z+beta.z]^d,
    A(theta)=s^d/product_(j=2)^d(1-theta_j).         (13)

The d positive numbers 1,1-theta_2,...,1-theta_d have arithmetic mean s. AM-GM therefore gives A(theta)>=1, with equality exactly at theta=0. This is exact angular optimization, rather than a second-order assertion. The same computation applies in every canonical chart by a vertex permutation.

On a common sufficiently small beta neighborhood, every bracket in F_r is positive. Its beta-Hessian is

    [d(d-1)/d!] sum_z [d r_z+beta.z]^(d-2) z z^T,

positive definite on L. At the baseline beta=0 its gradient is zero by sampled evenness. The implicit function theorem therefore gives the unique smooth critical beta(r) nearby, exactly characterized by (1). Strict convexity makes it the unique minimum on this common convex proper-cut neighborhood. Equation (13) proves that the full local normal minimum is tau(r), with canonical continuous direction.

For clarity, the angular Hessian of A at zero is

    I_(d-1)-(1/d) 11^T,

which is positive definite. Thus the full normal Hessian at each original minimizer is positive definite: its angular block is Q_0 times this matrix, its integer block is positive definite on L, and their mixed block vanishes in the coordinates (theta,beta).

The local formula is the actual GLOBAL all-normal minimum. The complete baseline menu and compact normal representation in Section 2 give a positive gap outside the canonical chart neighborhoods. Equation (8) preserves that gap uniformly for nearby bodies. Inside the neighborhoods the exact formula (13) and the unique strictly convex minimizer just proved give precisely (3) and (2). Thus no stationary cap is being treated as globally minimal without justification.

The competing-source gaps in Section 3 remain strict, and permutation averaging still gives (10). Within base 0, a nonzero x strictly improves on one shifted cap (3), by the same own-volume-loss argument. This proves actual global source uniqueness and all assertions concerning (1)--(3).

## 5. Actual critical slack families and ownership

At each nonzero base z_0, choose one ACTUAL attained minimizing cap at (z_0,0); existence follows from Section 2. Apply the full vertex-permutation group to it. All resulting caps have its same actual mass, strictly below tau(r), and its same raw integer coefficient alpha. Their continuous normals average to zero.

Their continuous normals span R^d. To check this without a representation-theory assumption, encode a nonzero normal by its d+1 vertex heights h_i, whose sum is zero and which are not all equal. Differences of two permutations exchanging unequal heights give nonzero multiples of coordinate differences in the zero-sum height space. Relabeling supplies every e_i-e_j, which span that d-dimensional space. The map from continuous normals to their vertex-height arrays is an isomorphism onto this space. Thus the full orbit is balanced and spans. It need not be a minimal circuit or have only d+1 members; no such unsupported claim is used.

At base z_0, if every orbit cap excluded a point, all its defining continuous values would be negative although their sum is zero. Hence this positive balanced family covers all of R^d at its own base. Assign it only that base. The active group (3) owns base 0. These finite assignments cover every original fiber, with strict auxiliary budgets.

Baseline auxiliary caps may be frozen for a smooth nearby covering menu, preserving exact incidence and own-base coverage and keeping their strict budget slack by (8). Such frozen caps need not stay critical. If genuine criticality at each new body is required, reselect a minimum there and take its finite orbit; no smooth selection is asserted. Shared original planes retain their one actual mass and are not replaced by independently varied copies. Every auxiliary critical cap has alpha.z_0>0, since otherwise it would contain the strictly deeper point Y.

## 6. Normalized mass and the exact zero-gain condition

The canonical beta=0 caps are feasible throughout the body neighborhood, so

    tau(r)<=F_r(0)=c_d sum_z r_z^d.                 (14)

In the common convex proper-cut chamber, strict convexity says equality holds exactly when beta(r)=0, or equivalently when its gradient at zero vanishes. This is precisely condition (5). No other normal branch can create a lower value, by Section 4. Scaling continuous coordinates by [Q_0/tau(r)]^(1/d) preserves the integer lattice and every fiber, and multiplies all cap masses by Q_0/tau(r). Scale integer normal coefficients by the same continuous factor to preserve cap incidence. The actual global raw depth becomes Q_0 and total mass becomes (4). Equation (14) proves its nonnegative gain and exact equality condition.

Thus (5) is the exact nearby nonlinear zero-gain surface. It is not silently replaced by its tangent equation when d>2.

## 7. Exact physical Hessian and its rank

All derivatives below are at the sampled even baseline. Set w_z=(r^0_z)^(d-2), G_w=sum w_z zz^T, and m=sum w_z v_z z. The constant c_d is as in Section 1. For the polynomial F in (13), the integer normal Hessian, body-normal mixed derivative, and frozen body Hessian are respectively

    K = c_d (d-1)G_w/d,
    b(v)=c_d(d-1)m,
    A[v,v]=c_d d(d-1)sum_z w_z v_z^2.               (15)

G_w is positive definite on L, since every w_z>0 and P spans L. Differentiating the attained first-order equation gives beta'[v]=-K^(-1)b(v)=-d G_w^dagger m. Hence the optimized cap Hessian is exactly

    tau''[v,v]
       =c_d d(d-1)[sum_z w_z v_z^2
                     -m^T G_w^dagger m].           (16)

The actual unnormalized total-volume Hessian is V_d d(d-1)sum w_z v_z^2. Its first variation equals tau'/Gamma_d, and its baseline value equals Q_0/Gamma_d. Differentiating the ratio in (4), these first-variation terms cancel, leaving

    M_tilde''=M''-tau''/Gamma_d.

Substitution proves (6), including its exact constant. The same formula holds for a C^2 compatible path with prescribed first velocity: the normalized mass first derivative vanishes in EVERY sampled-array direction, so acceleration terms do not enter.

The map v -> m is onto L, since for v_z=a.z its image is G_w a. Thus the quadratic form has rank k and kernel m=0 on the full sampled-array space. The form is not an assertion that every sampled velocity preserves concavity. The next section gives k explicit actually admissible directions realizing its positive rank.

## 8. Exact compatible affine escape and parity-neutral first order

For a in L, define r_a(z)=r^0(z)+a.z on all of B. Adding an affine function preserves concavity. Positivity persists for small a because B is compact and min_B r^0>0. This is therefore an actual two-sided body variation, even if the original radius has affine regions or lies on a boundary of the sampled concavity cone.

Take beta=-d a. Each bracket in (1) becomes d r^0_z, and its weighted sum against z is zero by baseline evenness. The local unique minimizer must therefore be beta(r_a)=-d a, and every active cap mass remains EXACTLY Q_0. The all-normal and competing-source theorems already proved show that this remains the actual global raw maximum.

The total mass is the polynomial in (7). Pair z and -z. Strict convexity of t^d on positive t gives

    (r^0_z+a.z)^d+(r^0_z-a.z)^d >2(r^0_z)^d

whenever a.z!=0. For nonzero a in L, at least one such pair exists. Hence mass strictly increases, proving (7) without any asymptotic error or unproved normalization step. The exact increment can alternatively be written as the sum of its positive even binomial terms.

Every affine direction has zero first total-volume derivative separately on each integer parity class: z and -z have the same parity and equal baseline weights (r^0_z)^(d-1), so their terms cancel. This fact records an explicit property of the admissible directions; it supplies no bound by 2^n on an arbitrary constrained positive index or ownership count.

### Exact invariance throughout the validated neighborhood

The same affine motion preserves the actual raw depth starting from ANY compatible r in this neighborhood, not only from the even baseline. As long as both arrays remain in the neighborhood,

    F_(r+a.z)(beta)=F_r(beta+d a).

Uniqueness of the minimizing branch and the all-normal theorem imply

    beta(r+a.z)=beta(r)-d a,
    tau(r+a.z)=tau(r).                              (17)

Both signs of small a are compatible. Strict convexity gives

    M(r+a.z)+M(r-a.z)>2M(r)  for a!=0 in L.

Therefore at least one of the two actual bodies has strictly greater mass and EXACTLY the same actual global raw depth. All auxiliary budgets remain slack for sufficiently small a by the proved source gaps. No point in this validated class can be a local maximum of total mass subject to that depth budget when k>0.

There is an exact finite-dimensional interpretation, also confined to this same neighborhood. For a sampled array r, define

    J_r(a)=sum_z |r_z+a.z|^d,  a in L.

The map a -> (a.z)_(z in P) is injective on L. Thus J_r is strictly convex and coercive: the triangle inequality gives ||r+(a.z)||_d >= ||(a.z)||_d-||r||_d, and the first norm is bounded below by a positive constant times |a|. J_r has a unique global minimizer. At the even baseline that minimizer is zero, by its vanishing gradient. Its minimizer tends to zero as r tends to r^0: uniform coercivity bounds every minimizing sequence, and any subsequential limit minimizes the strictly convex baseline functional. Consequently all its residual entries are positive for r near r^0. Its first-order equation is then exactly (1), with beta=d a. Hence

    tau(r)=c_d min_(a in L) sum_z |r_z+a.z|^d.       (18)

This is the d-th power of the ordinary l_d distance from the sampled radius array to the subspace of functions z -> a.z, multiplied by c_d. There is NO constant term in this subspace. Equation (18) is a proved local description of this actual geometric family, not an assumed functional inequality for arbitrary fibers.

## 9. Scope and boundary cases

All geometry is actual, all source points lie in S_r, every original fiber is retained, and all ambient halfspaces are considered. Closed vertical halfspaces with boundary fiber mass were explicitly dominated by actual finite nonvertical cuts. The common projection and positive radii prevent empty-fiber changes and lower-dimensional contributions in this local class. Rank-deficient P uses L and G_w^dagger, so invisible integer normal components cannot create a spurious strict Hessian.

If P={0}, then k=0, beta is absent, tau=c_d r_0^d, and normalization keeps total mass fixed. This includes n=0. The result deliberately assumes d>=2. For d=1, affine-radius mass changes cancel exactly across a symmetric base and the integer-normal curvature used here vanishes; no false positive-rank escape is claimed there.

At the baseline the normalized maximum is Gamma_d, whereas the OC target for n>=1 is Gamma_d/2^n. The theorem describes a local decrease from that above-target family. It does not imply that the same normal menu, competing-source gap, or compatible escape exists at an arbitrary below-target candidate.
